transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~70 minutes | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luca (Redwood SE), Sofia (Hartwell Head Cloud Sec), Daniel (Infra), Aisha (Compliance), Ben (SRE)

Summary (auto): Deep dive on Private/VPC deployment model, network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs and KMS/BYOK. Discussed SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SIEM integration, and on-prem/air-gapped considerations. Agreed to share docs and schedule install walkthrough.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick check — audio good?
[00:10] Sofia: yep, good here. thanks, Evan.
[00:15] Evan: cool. i'll hand to Priya and Luca to run the architecture deep dive, but first quick context — Hartwell is evaluating Private VPC model for strict data residency and to avoid public egress, right?
[00:28] Sofia: yes, exact. we need to ensure no customer data leaves our vpc, retention meets SOC two standards, and we can integrate with our okta/rbac.
[00:40] Priya: great. we'll run through high level then dive network specifics — control plane options (private control plane vs managed), ingress patterns, egress restrictions, and encryption/KMS. we'll also cover audit logs and integrations (cloudtrail, vpc flow logs, SIEM). note: transcription may swap some acronyms.
[00:58] Luca: quick note — when we say Private deployment here, we mean Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink; the compute runs in your VPC or on-prem, and control plane is optionally customer-managed for air-gap scenarios.
[01:15] Daniel: can you clarify "control plane" — does Redwood still see telemetry? we need to minimize outbound telemetry for regulatory reasons.
[01:25] Priya: yes. there are two options — (1) Hosted control plane with a private egress tunnel (we can restrict telemetry endpoints and use egress via your NAT or allowlist), (2) Fully private control plane where the control plane runs in your environment — typical for air-gapped. In the fully private mode telemetry is optional and can be disabled; you keep full audit logs locally.
[01:48] Ben: if telemetry is disabled, how do you handle updates/rollouts and health checks?
[01:55] Luca: Updates are either pulled from an approved artifact repository you host, or pushed during scheduled maintenance windows via an outbound connection you control. Health checks can be mediated via a bastion or an internal monitoring relay. we document the patterns.
[02:12] Sofia: let's jump into network isolation. our security policy says no public IPs on inference servers and egress only allowed to a small set of destinations. how do you handle ingress and egress?
[02:25] Priya: typically we support three main patterns:
- PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint: Redwood exposes a VPC Endpoint service (or we consume yours) so traffic never traverses the public internet.
- VPC Peering / Transit Gateway: for high throughput we can peer into your VPC or use TGW.
- On-prem direct install: for air-gapped, we install on your hardware behind your firewalls.
(we sometimes use a combination — e.g., PrivateLink for control plane, peering for data plane).
[03:05] Daniel: firewalling? port lists?
[03:09] Priya: we'll share a port list but high level: TLS 443 for API, gRPC ports for internal agent comms (configurable), health/metrics endpoints restricted to internal CIDRs, and SSH only for break-glass via a bastion with strict RBAC and key rotation. we recommend no inbound from internet to compute nodes, all egress goes through your NAT or VPC endpoints.
[03:35] Daniel: what about egress to model artifact stores or third-party telemetry? we do not want any third-party storage access.
[03:41] Luca: you can host model artifacts in your S3 or internal blob store. Redwood can pull from S3 via VPC endpoint with IAM role access. for third-party telemetry we can turn off telemetry collection entirely or route it to your SIEM via syslog/http forwarder.
[03:58] Ben: VPC flow logs and CloudTrail — can Redwood ship logs to our S3 bucket or do we pull?
[04:05] Priya: both. options: push logs to your S3 or Kinesis with customer credentials, or you can pull log bundles via a secure endpoint. for compliance, pushing to your own storage tends to be simpler.
[04:18] Aisha: retention windows — SOC2 wants at least 12 months for some artifacts, do you support custom retention?
[04:24] Priya: yes, audit log retention is configurable. by default Redwood stores a shorter window for hosted, but in Private we support shipping and retaining logs in your storage for whatever window you define — 12 months, 24 months, etc. we'll include retention controls in the deployment runbook.
[04:40] Sofia: RBAC and SSO — we use Okta, need SCIM provisioning, group mapping, and SAML SSO. how do users and roles map to Redwood's admin/ops roles?
[04:51] Luca: we integrate with Okta via SAML SSO and SCIM. you map Okta groups to Redwood roles: viewer, operator, admin. RBAC is enforced locally in the control plane and audit events include user ids and group membership. we also support mutual TLS for service accounts.
[05:08] Daniel: can we enforce attribute-based access (e.g., restrict model deployment to infra group)?
[05:13] Priya: yes, we support fine-grained role policies and can bind actions like model deployment, rollout, and config changes to groups. we can sample policies during the PoC.
[05:24] Sofia: encryption at rest and KMS — we require BYOK with HSM-backed keys. is that supported?
[05:31] Luca: yes, BYOK supported. two modes: integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys, Google CSMK, Azure Key Vault HSM) or a local HSM appliance for on-prem. keys never leave your KMS; Redwood performs envelope encryption and uses ephemeral data keys for disk encryption.
[05:52] Ben: do you store unencrypted model weights anywhere?
[05:55] Priya: no, weights at rest are encrypted. in Private deployment, models are stored in your artifact store encrypted with your keys. Redwood only accesses decrypted models in memory at runtime; swap/eviction policy logs are recorded.
[06:10] Aisha: audit logs must include key usage and access to decrypted data — do you capture that?
[06:16] Luca: yes, KMS access events are logged. when a key unwrap operation occurs we log key id, principal, timestamp, and the action. that gets forwarded to your CloudTrail or SIEM.
[06:28] Sofia: network ACLs vs security groups — any recommendations?
[06:31] Priya: security groups for instance-level controls, NACLs for subnet-level defense-in-depth. we provide recommended security group templates and NACL templates. for strict environments, do deny rules at NACL plus restrictive SGs. we also recommend private route tables that avoid internet gateway attachments for subnets with compute.
[06:53] Daniel: what about egress filtering — we need to enforce allowlist only.
[06:57] Priya: enforce at NAT or proxy layer — egress to artifact stores via VPC endpoints, to KMS endpoints via VPC endpoint, and block 0.0.0.0/0. For external dependencies (like OS updates) you can either provide an internal package mirror or a proxy that allows vetted endpoints.
[07:18] Ben: patching — how do you handle CVE updates in an air-gapped install?
[07:22] Luca: we provide signed artifact bundles that you pull into your update repository. for emergency CVEs we have an expedited process where we provide signed hotfix images that you can stage via your offline transfer process.
[07:36] Sofia: compliance — do you provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation for the product?
[07:42] Evan: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs and the related control matrices. in Private mode we also provide the deployment runbook and a customer-specific responsibility matrix.
[07:55] Aisha: can we get a control mapping doc showing which controls are customer vs vendor?
[07:59] Evan: absolutely, we'll include a shared RACI-style matrix.
[08:05] Daniel: logging volume — if we enable debug event capture, will that balloon storage costs?
[08:10] Priya: yes, debug logs are verbose. we recommend default info-level with structured fields; debug can be gated to a short window and shipped to your hot storage. everything is configurable.
[08:22] Sofia: SIEM integration specifics — Splunk and SumoLogic are in use: can you push logs to those?
[08:27] Luca: yes, we support forwarding via Kinesis/Firehose, syslog, or HTTP event collectors. for Splunk we can push to HEC with your token. we also support Kafka for high-throughput setups.
[08:40] Ben: what about network performance for embeddings/high-throughput calls — peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs?
[08:46] Priya: peering or TGW provides lower latency and high throughput; PrivateLink is simpler from security posture (no route table changes in your VPC) but can add small network overhead. for high QPS, peering/TGW is recommended.
[09:00] Daniel: can we do TLS mutual auth on the data plane?
[09:04] Luca: yes mutual TLS for service-to-service is supported; we can also do TLS with client cert validation for admin APIs.
[09:12] Sofia: backup and disaster recovery — disks encrypted, snapshots — who controls?
[09:18] Priya: in Private, snapshots are taken into your account and encrypted with your keys; retention and replication are configured per your policy. for on-prem we integrate with your backup tooling.
[09:32] Aisha: do you have penetration test reports?
[09:36] Evan: we have third-party pentest summary reports we can share under NDA along with remediation timelines.
[09:42] Sofia: air-gapped deployment specifics — we need to know exactly which ports to open during install and which artifacts to stage.
[09:50] Luca: install requires outbound to our artifact signing endpoint to validate signatures unless you choose full offline validation; minimal ports for admin console can be tunneled via bastion. we'll provide an install checklist: artifact list, checksums, signature keys, and an install runbook.
[10:05] Ben: how about ephemeral credentials for model execution? we don't want long-lived service accounts on nodes.
[10:11] Priya: we use short-lived tokens and rotate them frequently. for cloud we use instance roles combined with short-lived session tokens. for on-prem we can integrate with your Vault for dynamic secrets.
[10:22] Daniel: any support for hardware attestation (TPM, Nitro Enclaves)?
[10:26] Luca: we can integrate with Nitro Enclaves for sensitive key operations on AWS and with TPM-based attestation for on-prem. support varies by deployment mode but it's on the roadmap for stronger attestation.
[10:40] Sofia: operational runbooks — who has access to them? we want runbooks to be embargoed and only accessible to our infra admins.
[10:48] Evan: runbooks are shared via a secure portal and access is controlled by the same SSO/SCIM rules you define; we can gate sections to particular groups.
[10:56] Aisha: change control — do you support canary rollouts and automatic rollback on regressions?
[11:00] Priya: yes we support canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model versions. those actions are audited and can be restricted by RBAC.
[11:12] Daniel: network testing — will Redwood help with traffic shaping and e2e perf tests in our VPC?
[11:17] Luca: yes, we typically run a benchmarking engagement during PoC: synthetic load generators hosted in your VPC, traces, and tail-latency measurements. we'll share a perf plan.
[11:30] Ben: final question on legal — we need a data processing addendum (DPA) and standard contractual clauses for cross-border data flows.
[11:38] Evan: we have a DPA template and can include SCCs. for Bank customers we recommend Private deployment which minimizes cross-border flows because you can keep all data in your region.
[11:50] Sofia: ok, thanks. let's recap next steps.
[11:54] Evan: recap: Evan to share SOC2/ISO and pentest summary; Priya to send port list / SG templates / sample terraform; we'll provide RACI matrix; schedule install walkthrough — propose next Thursday; Hartwell to provide CIDRs and point of contact for infra.
[12:12] Aisha: that works — i'll confirm internal availability and also confirm retention window questions.
[12:19] Daniel: i'll collate the network ranges and send over the TGW plan.
[12:23] Evan: great, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite. thanks everyone.
